title: Mako SE implementation playbook - AcmeHealth
content:
Context / quick summary:
- Customer: AcmeHealth (regulated healthcare SaaS). Needs private deployment in eu-west1 with HSM integration and strict audit logs.
- Target model: open model family (cust-wrapped vicuna-13b), target runtime quant: q4_0 or q4_1 depending on perf tests. Primary route: dedicated GPU pool (reserved) + fallback to hosted-lowcost for bursts.
- Constraints: no external egress for model weights, EKM/HSM for keys, VPC peering to their analytics VPC, 3-month rolling audit retention for logs.
- Primary contact: Claire (Acme infra), Sec contact: Henrik.

Objectives for this sprint (high level):
- Get PoC private control plane up in their dev VPC (eu-west1).
- Wire HSM for KMS integration and validate key rotation with compliance.
- Create rollout plan: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic fallback and alerting.
- Perf run: baseline latency P50/P95 with seq len 512 and batch sizes [1,4,8].

Notes / config bits (working):
- Cluster sizing (initial): pool of 4 x A100-40GB equiv / or 6x A10G if cheaper and model fits. Priority: throughput + KV cache memory.
- Suggested Dedicated config:
  * reserved_units: 4
  * autoscale: min:4 max:8 burst:2
  * model_variant: vicuna-13b-q4_0 (fallback: vicuna-13b-fp16-hosted)
- redwoodctl snippets (dev cluster):
  # apply private control plane skeleton
  redwoodctl deploy private --org acmehealth --region eu-west1 --env dev --confirmation auto

  # attach HSM/KMS
  redwoodctl kms attach --cluster acme-dev --provider hsm --uri \"gcp-kms://projects/acme/locations/global/keyRings/rdw/cryptoKeys/rdw-key\"

- Network / firewall: must allow inbound from AcmeProd NAT ranges on 10.10.0.0/16 -> control plane port 443, metrics port 9090 (only from monitoring VPC). Validate with their infra team on 2026-03-03.
- IAM roles: create service principal se-acme-deploy with roles: redwood.clusterAdmin, redwood.kmsUser, logging.write. Add short-lived tokens for admins (rotate daily during canary).

Test plan & perf checklist:
- Perf harness: use bench/vicuna-runner with seq=512; runs: qps ramp 5 -> 200 over 30m windows, capture P50/P95/P99 and GPU util.
- Baseline targets: P50 < 120ms (seq256), P95 < 450ms (seq512), cost per 1k tokens target < $X (placeholder).
- Functional tests: prompt-set “acme-clinical-100” (sensitive PII-like content), ensure response redaction & policy chains works in private mode.
- Eval: quick automated prompt coverage runner -> store results in stackdriver and S3 snapshot.

Rollout plan / safeguards:
- Canary: route 2% of traffic (internal clients only) for 24h, health checks: error rate < 0.5%, latency SLO pass, no PII leakage alerts.
- Auto-fallback if: error_rate > 0.8% for 10m or avg GPU temp > 85C for 5m. Fallback targets: hosted vicuna-fp16 or smaller 7b hosted variant.
- Monitoring: add dashboards: token-cost, per-route latency, per-instance GPU mem, KV cache hit rate. Alert channels -> #se-acme, ops oncall, pager if severity >= P1.

Action items (personal TODOs) - live log:
- [ ] 2026-02-28: Draft initial infra plan and sizing (DONE)
- [ ] 2026-03-01: Share draft with Eng Infra + Security (IN PROGRESS) -> asked Sofia to review network section.
- [ ] 2026-03-03: Call with Acme infra to confirm VPC and NAT ranges (scheduled)
- [ ] 2026-03-04: Run first perf tests on dev pool (blocked until HSM attached)
- [ ] 2026-03-06: Implement canary traffic routing rules (redwood routing policy)
- [ ] 2026-03-08: Security review signoff (depends on HSM rotation test)
- [ ] 2026-03-10: Deliver PoC report + perf numbers to Claire (target)

Things I'm uncertain about / decisions to make:
- HSM latency impact: need to quantify additional ms for key unwrap per request; might need caching of DEKs for short TTL. Follow up: ask infra security for HSM latency numbers (Tomás to ping vendor).
- Quantization choice: q4_0 likely best balance, but if accuracy regression > 1.5% on clinical prompt set, fallback to q4_1 or fp16. Need to run eval on our eval harness.
- Logs retention window: compliance asks 90 days immutable; our platform default 30d. Proposal: send immutable copies to their S3/GCS bucket daily. Confirm with Sec.

Quick notes from last sync (2026-03-02 standup):
- Sofia: will draft network ACLs and sample Terraform for peering.
- Priya: working on policy chains to detect PII leakage for Acme prompt set.
- Tomás: contacting HSM vendor for perf numbers and rotation API details.
- Claire: requested a list of mitigation steps if model misbehaves (we have rollback + fallback + throttling).

Local scratch commands (put here for quick copy):
- redwoodctl route create acme-canary --cluster acme-dev --percent 2 --policy canary --fallback vicuna-13b-fp16-hosted
- redwoodctl scale cluster acme-dev --replicas 4 --instance-type a10g
- gcloud compute networks peerings create acme-peer --network=rdw-private --peer-project=acme-prod --peer-network=acme-vpc

Notes for handoff to Delivery Eng (what they need to validate):
- Confirm HA on control-plane (3 replicas) and DB backup schedule (daily).
- Verify KV cache persistence across restarts for warm-cache performance.
- Confirm HSM rotation can be triggered without downtime (playbook + runbook).
- Provide traffic replay tool + stored prompt traces (PII scrubbed) for validation.

Open questions to raise in next sync:
- Are we comfortable with initial pool size or should we upsell reserved_units to 6 given peak QPS?
- Can Acme accept 7-day TTL for DEKs to reduce HSM calls? Security tradeoff.

End-of-day quick personal notes:
- Keep this doc as living scratchpad. Move stable configs to private-deploy-configs repo once validated.
- Follow up items: get vendor HSM latency, finalize canary percent with Claire, push terraform sample to PR #229.

-- Arjun (scratchpad)
